intro: ThinkSystem versions roll out over several years. A V3 badge is a platform-family label, not proof the particular server launched in 2022. Use the model’s dated announcement or first public guide below to separate its own age from the wider generation.

generations.label: Original ThinkSystem
generations.summary: The ThinkSystem brand launched in June 2017. Original SR630/SR650-era names often omit “V1”; an unsuffixed name does not establish the launch year of every model.

generations.label: ThinkSystem V2
generations.summary: Scale-up SR850 V2/SR860 V2 were announced in June 2020. The broader SR630 V2/SR650 V2 rack and ST650 V2 tower wave followed in April 2021.

generations.label: ThinkSystem V3
generations.summary: V3 was announced as a portfolio in September 2022. Individual models followed in 2022–2024; qualified EPYC 9005 refreshes arrived in 2024 without changing V3 to V4.

generations.label: ThinkEdge SE455 V3
generations.summary: This edge model was unveiled in September 2023. Its own introduction is later than the 2022 V3 portfolio milestone.

generations.label: ThinkSystem V4
generations.summary: V4 began with a June 2024 portfolio announcement. SR630 V4 documentation followed that year; SR650 V4 and SR650a V4 were announced in February 2025.

generations.label: SC750 V4 Neptune
generations.summary: SC750 V4 was announced in September 2024. Neptune cooling predates this model; V4 and Neptune technology generations are different labels.

generations.label: ThinkEdge SE100
generations.summary: SE100 was announced in March 2025. Its model name does not use the ThinkSystem V3/V4 version sequence.

sr630.note: First public product guide: September 2024. The February 2025 announcement added P-core configurations; the V4 model already existed with E-core options.

sr650.note: Announced February 2025, after the V4 portfolio’s June 2024 debut. The first product guide carries the same February date.

sr650a.note: Announced February 2025, after the V4 portfolio’s June 2024 debut. The first product guide carries the same February date.

sr635.note: First public guide: February 2023. The later EPYC 9005 qualification refresh does not change the server name from V3.

sr655.note: First public guide: February 2023. The later EPYC 9005 qualification refresh does not change the server name from V3.

sr645.note: First public guide: November 2022. EPYC 9005 support is a later CPU refresh within this V3 platform.

sr665.note: First public guide: November 2022. EPYC 9005 support is a later CPU refresh within this V3 platform.

sr860.note: First public guide: July 2025. This four-socket model followed the initial 2024 V4 portfolio announcement.

st45.note: First public guide: December 2024 with EPYC 4004. The October 2025 change history adds EPYC 4005 CPUs; V3 does not mean this tower launched in 2022.

st650.note: First public guide: May 2023. Qualified 5th Gen Xeon options are a later refresh of the same V3 tower.

se455.note: Unveiled September 2023; its first product guide followed in October. The later SE455i inference configuration is distinct from the original model introduction.

se100.note: Announced March 2025; first full product guide published April 2025. It has its own model timeline without a V3/V4 suffix.

sd535.note: First public guide: April 2024. The October 2024 update added EPYC 9005 support; this V3 dense node is newer than the first 2022 V3 models.

sc750.note: Announced September 2024; the full product guide followed in October. This dates SC750 V4, not the first use of Neptune liquid cooling.

sr675.note: First public guide: November 2022. GPU shuttles, EPYC 9005 support and named inference configurations were expanded later.

sr685a.note: First public guide: April 2024. Its September 2026 withdrawal notice is a lifecycle event, not its introduction date.

sr680a.note: First public guide: September 2025. This eight-GPU V4 model followed the initial 2024 V4 portfolio rollout.

sd665.note: First public guide: 10 November 2022. EPYC 9005 qualification was added 10 October 2024 within V3; this dates the model, not the first use of Neptune cooling.

sr665original.note: The SR665 guide was first published 5 May 2020. Original ThinkSystem family launch in 2017 is not this model’s introduction year.
